title: dffram.py fails at step STA
body:
Hi,

I'm having troubles generating any DFFRAM from the set of supported parameters, e.g. 128x32.
I tried the DFFRAM main branch and also checked out tag 0.0.1, getting seemingly the same result.

The sky130A PDK (latest) is installed under:
```
$>echo $PDK_ROOT
/opt/open_pdks/share/pdk
```
The PDK appears to be recognized, since `./dffram.py -s 128x32` starts running through synthesis etc., but then fails at static timing analysis.
On the first run of `dffram.py` the docker image `efabless/openlane:2021.10.25_20.35.00` was pulled. There is also a docker image named `dffram-env:latest`, but I didn't catch where it came from...

Here are the steps I have taken:

comments.body:
Hey- so for background: `dffram-env:latest` is an ad hoc image that was built and used by some older versions of dffram, but is no longer needed.

This STA failure looks like a memory error of some kind: if you're using the latest PDK, that'd be the cause, as we do have a confirmed issue with that particular PDK: see https://github.com/The-OpenROAD-Project/OpenROAD/issues/1305 for more info. We'll ping you when there's an available fix in OpenLane.

title: CPU hangs up when accessing memory just below MMIO address space

comments.body:
Hi imhcyx,
this bug is probably because access request at 0x7fffffc0 in L2 CacheStage3 was blocked and accidently flushed by the prefetch request in Stage2. Now we have fixed this bug in prefetcher so L2 Cache will not be accessed if the prefetch request is mapped into MMIO space in branch "bug-prefetch-mmio". Please let us know if works in your FPGA board and thanks for pointing out the problem!

@ZLJ987 
Seems the problem still exists...
@imhcyx Would you please have a try with the prefetcher disabled?

title: Unable to synthesize the design in Vivado 2021.2
body:
Hi, I'm compling the design into Verilog with command `make PRJ=myproject BOARD=pynq STANDALONE=true` and with default settings. However, the compiled code contains some depth-1 array in the `EmbeddedTLBMD` module, and when I synthesize the code with Vivado 2021.2, it says `[Synth 8-2913] Unsupported Dual Port Block-RAM template for tlbmd_3_reg` and reasons to cause this error contains `Write port has constant address.` and `Only 1 word in RAM `. These are both true. Array `tlbmd_0` to `tlbmd_3` does have only one element and address input is constant (beacuse the entry count of the ITLB declared in [NutCore.scala](https://github.com/OSCPU/NutShell/blob/cf7963435b824106690152507bb9312c159b8d5e/src/main/scala/nutcore/NutCore.scala#L116) is only 4, so `depth of the array` = [TotalEntry / Ways](https://github.com/OSCPU/NutShell/blob/cf7963435b824106690152507bb9312c159b8d5e/src/main/scala/nutcore/mem/TLB.scala#L161) = 1).

A simple way to fix this problem is by manually adding a platform-specific attribute `ram_style` to these signals repectively, and set the values to `registers`, as follows, so the arrays can be implemented with registers. (I don't know if the line contains the attribute can be added without users' intervention (by Chisel comilers))
``` Verilog
  (* ram_style = "registers" *) 
  reg [120:0] tlbmd_0 [0:0];
```
The `ram_style` attribute is also abled to be set using elaberation-time constrains, however an additional XDC file is required in this situation. I'm not sure which is the most appropiate approach to solve the problem.


The following is `EmbeddedTLBMD` module in the generated code, and only the array `tlbmd_0` to `tlbmd_3` are related to the issue.
``` Verilog
module EmbeddedTLBMD(
  input          clock,

);

title: Wrong assignment to enum variable from expression of different type
body:
Hey!
 Enum should be assignment only by enum type. LRM1800-2017 6.19.4: `A cast shall be required for an expression that is assigned to an enum variable where the type of the expression is not equivalent to the enumeration type of the variable.`
So in file ` design/ifu/ifu_ifc_ctl.sv` need to be change two lines:
`   assign next_state[1] = (~state[1] & state[0] & ~reset_delayed & miss_f2 & ~goto_idle) |
                          (state[1] & ~reset_delayed & ~mb_empty_mod & ~goto_idle);`
 for
`   assign next_state[1] = state_t'((~state[1] & state[0] & ~reset_delayed & miss_f2 & ~goto_idle) |
                          (state[1] & ~reset_delayed & ~mb_empty_mod & ~goto_idle));`

and
`   assign next_state[0] = (~goto_idle & leave_idle) | (state[0] & ~goto_idle) |
                          (reset_delayed);`
for
`   assign next_state[0] = state_t'((~goto_idle & leave_idle) | (state[0] & ~goto_idle) |
                          (reset_delayed));`
Like was done in pull request #49

comments.body: Thanks for reporting this, and #62. RTL will be fixed in the next release.

title: [TTI] Spurious TX_DESC_STAT interrupt caused by virtual_device_sel_i gap on bus START
body: Hi i3c-core team, We're using [i3c-v1.5.0](https://github.com/chipsalliance/i3c-core/releases/tag/i3c-v1.5.0) and found spurious TX_DESC_STAT interrupt caused by virtual_device_sel_i gap on bus START **New version** i3c-core/src/hci/tti.sv: [line 427](https://github.com/chipsalliance/i3c-core/blob/db4a6f341145e05a5b7002a21d1cd5cc31147f35/src/hci/tti.sv#L427) `.irq_i (~virtual_device_sel_i & tx_pr_start_i), // Per-transaction flag` **The Race Condition** virtual_device_sel_i is **cleared on every Start condition** (i3c_target_fsm.sv, [line 871](https://github.com/chipsalliance/i3c-core/blob/db4a6f341145e05a5b7002a21d1cd5cc31147f35/src/ctrl/i3c_target_fsm.sv#L871) ): ``` else if (bus_any_start_det || bus_stop_det_i) begin virtual_device_sel_o <= '0; // ← Clears on Start! ``` On every bus START condition, virtual_device_sel_o is forced to 0. It only reasserts after the FSM enters CheckFByte/CheckSByte and the address matches. During this multi-cycle gap, ~virtual_device_sel_i is 1, **which opens the interrupt gate and allows TX_DESC_STAT to fire spuriously if tx_pr_start_i is asserted**. **Waveform** Thanks, TJ

fix_commits.messageHeadline: [src] Align virtual_device_sel with other control signals (#217)

comments.body:
Hi @TJTseng 

What is the context of this use case in a system view? 

If it is in Caliptra's context, while streaming boot is ongoing, i3c interrupts are not enabled. The way streaming boot agent running on BMC would know to enumerate over mctp is after streaming boot is completed. It is after the streaming boot is done that the interrupts can be enabled as a part of indicating the completion of streaming boot. 

Since the MCTP that runs on one target is mutually exclusive with the recovery flow, as in streaming boot completes and then mctp starts, streaming boot transactions are not expected to come from the streaming boot agent (that runs on BMC or something equivalent of BMC) once Caliptra SS indicates the completion.

In summary, while this interrupt assertion is getting triggered, in the specific system flow where this is applied, there is no scenario that this becomes relevant. Having said that, it is an odd behavior that we will fix in future revision.

Please let me know if you have any questions.

Hi @bharatpillilli ,
Thank you for the detailed explanation. Currently, we don't have this scenario in our system flow. We observed the odd behavior because we accidentally enabled TX_DESC_STAT_EN during recovery mode, so we reported this issue in case of any side effects. Our current approach is to disable TX_DESC_STAT_EN during recovery mode.

Let me summarize my understanding to make sure we're on the same page:
 Recovery / I3C streaming boot:
  - virtual_device_sel_i is active during this phase, and the transient deassertion on bus START creates the interrupt gating window
  - However, TX_DESC_STAT_EN should not be enabled during this phase, so the spurious interrupt does not fire

  MCTP (post-boot management communication):
  - Runs on the primary I3C target address, not the virtual target address
  - virtual_device_sel_i is not involved in MCTP transactions, so the gating issue does not apply

Are these correct?

Thanks,
TJ

@TJTseng 

Your assumptions are correct. 

We are marking this as a feature enhancement since interrupts are not supposed to be enabled during recovery flow. This enhancement will be in our next I3C release. Please make sure to follow these guidelines:

1. During recovery mode they shall be no private reads/writes to the main target
2. During recovery mode FW must disable interrupts (including TX_DESC_STAT)
3. When exiting recovery mode FW must clear TX_DESC_STAT interrupts.
     a. Once recovery mode has been exited the controller shall not issue any OCP recovery commands - there is not live status to read.

This enhancement has been integrated into the v1p6 branch https://github.com/chipsalliance/i3c-core/pull/217

I will close this issue in 1 week pending any additional questions.

title: Should the default JTAG IDCODE be 0x1?
body:
https://github.com/freechipsproject/rocket-chip/blob/9002e7e53299598027f41b95dba1666310923699/src/main/scala/rocketchip/DebugTransport.scala#L22

```scala
class JtagDTMKeyDefault extends JtagDTMConfig(
  idcodeVersion = 0,
  idcodePartNum = 0,
  idcodeManufId = 0,
debugIdleCycles = 5) // Reasonable guess for synchronization.
```

Should the default IDCODE be 0x1, or the same as in the previous debug module (0x10e31913)? Or should it throw an error message to prevent rocket from elaborating if the JTAG is enabled but the idcode is not specified?

@mwachs5 @palmer-dabbelt @ducky64

fix_commits.messageHeadline: Add a note to wire up jtag_mfr_id
Add a note to wire up jtag_mfr_id (#778)

comments.body:
The IDCODE (0x10e31913) uses SiFive's assigned JEDEC Manufacturer ID. So in general those who aren't SiFive should not be using that IDCODE. That's why we removed it from the default.

Those using rocket-chip repo should probably override this default value to something meaningful for their design. The ManufId is actually exported from the ExampleTop as part of its I/O and is tied off in the TestHarness.

I see, that makes sense. Thanks for the explanation. Would having an elaboration-time warning for users of rocket-chip be useful so that they don't run into surprises when they try to program their cores?

When you say "program their cores" do you mean when using OpenOCD to communicate with them? Is there actually a value that you use there that causes a problem? riscv-openocd is very tolerant of the IDCODE, it may print a warning if it's not the expected ID.

I'm not sure what the elaboration time warning would be because the mfr_id could go all the way out the pins of the chip. I added a runtime warning (so if you ran with simulate it could at least detect illegal idcodes, though the chances you detect an unconnected mfr_id are somewhat low):

https://github.com/freechipsproject/rocket-chip/blob/master/src/main/scala/jtag/JtagTap.scala#L175

Note that if you did actually use the defaults here, then your IDCODE *would* be 0x1, because there is a bit in the IDCODE "always 1":
https://github.com/freechipsproject/rocket-chip/blob/master/src/main/scala/rocketchip/DebugTransport.scala#L230

@mwachs5 Ah, I see. I think I see where my confusion was coming from now.

In https://github.com/freechipsproject/rocket-chip/blob/9002e7e53299598027f41b95dba1666310923699/src/main/scala/rocketchip/DebugTransport.scala#L231 it uses two out of the three `Int`s in `JtagDTMConfig` but doesn't actually 
use the third one. I was confused since I thought that all 3 would be determined at elaboration-time by `JtagDTMConfig`. In my design, I think I left io.jtag_mfr_id unconnected and the synthesis tool tied it at some point to zero.

Perhaps if we are not actually going to use `c.idcodeManufId.U`, perhaps it could be a good idea to put in a comment saying "Please wire up io.jtag_mfr_id to set the mfr_id or something"? The TestHarness I think manually goes and re-retrieves it (or maybe just remove `idcodeManufId` from `JtagDTMConfig` to avoid confusion perhaps).

```scala
  idcode.always1    := 1.U
  idcode.version    := c.idcodeVersion.U
  idcode.partNumber := c.idcodePartNum.U
  idcode.mfrId := io.jtag_mfr_id
```

The comment seems like a reasonable request. Keep in mind that RocketChipExampleTop is just an example top level, and other designs could actually wire up mfrId using the value in JtagDTMConfig,  I think we should leave it there but comment it as you suggest.
Thoughts on https://github.com/freechipsproject/rocket-chip/pull/778 ?

title: Rocket comes out of reset with valid icache data
body:
Certain randomization values can lead to rocket's icache immediately asserting a valid response. In default rocket-chip configurations this doesn't have any affect on the processor because a debug interrupt comes before the processor is ready to begin executing. But if you were to use a tethered interface to bring up the system there would be no need for the debug interrupt at the start.

My issue then becomes a question:
Should I setup mtvec or similar mechanism before the processor is reset? 
Can I rely on the first instruction at the reset vector to be fetched correctly? 

If this is simply a bug my current fix to this issue for me is the following diff in icache.scala

```
-      val s2_hit = RegEnable(s1_hit, !stall)
+      val s2_hit = RegEnable(s1_hit, Bool(false), !stall)
```

I think @aswaterman would be the best one to answer this question.

comments.body: How many ticks of clock are you asserting with reset high (need to assert several to "flush" the pipeline)?

Probably a couple hundred thousand. In my environment the coreplex comes out of reset first and then the program is loaded via a tether, after all that is done rocket's reset is lowered. So its definitely in reset for long enough. Let me get you a seed and hash of rocket-chip that presents the problem for me.
I used the random_seed 894732643 in vcs with the rocket-chip hash ee66fd28eba3f6a9479d209240dc7fb33d11c8a8
For the whole time reset is asserted you should see that the icache is asserting valid.
I'll try to reproduce but think I need more than just the seed and hash... would your CONFIG/testbench impact the randomization?
This is clean rocket-chip on that hash with the default config

title: PTW incorrectly marks the access fault type for out-of-range non-leaf PTEs
body:
<!-- THIS REPOSITORY'S ISSUES ARE RESERVED FOR FEATURE REQUESTS AND BUG REPORTS. -->
<!-- For support questions related to Rocket Chip, please use [Stack Overflow [rocket-chip]](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/rocket-chip). -->
<!-- For support questions related to Chisel, please use [Stack Overflow [chisel]](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/chisel). -->
<!-- Please select the item best describing the issue in each category and delete the other items. -->

<!-- choose all that apply -->
**Type of issue**: bug report

<!-- choose one -->
**Impact**: unknown

<!-- choose one -->
**Development Phase**: proposal

**Other information**
 <!-- include detailed explanation, stacktraces, related issues, suggestions how to fix, links for us to have context, eg. Stack Overflow, gitter, etc -->

**If the current behavior is a bug, please provide the steps to reproduce the problem:**
In S mode, the PTW gets a valid, non-leaf PTE with a PPN exceeding the physical address space.

**What is the current behavior?**
Rocket-chip checks the PPNs (`!invalid_paddr` in PTW.scala:316) before traversing to the next level of page table. It thens returns `ae_final` to the TLB. However, since the page is non-leaf, it does not have the `r` bit set. Therefore, further a read request to TLB is responded with a page-fault exception.

**What is the expected behavior?**
According to the RISC-V manual 5.3.2, in step 4, if the PTE is valid and `pte.r = 0` and `pte.x = 0`, the PTE is a pointer to the next level of page table. Since we have not finished the three levels of page table, we continue to step 2 and `a = pte.ppn X PAGESIZE` to calculate the base address. If accessing the PTE violates the PMA, it should raise an access-fault exception.

This is the same behavior as in Spike. As seen in `mmu_t::walk`, if the PTE points to the next level of page table and does not have any bits of `PTE_D | PTE_A | PTE_U | PTE_N | PTE_PBMT` set, then we calculate the next base address with `base = ppn << PGSHIFT;` and continue to the next iteration of the for loop. In the next level, if accessing the PTE violates PMA (like exceeding the physical address space), an access-fault exception is raised.


**Please tell us about your environment:**
<!--    (examples)
    - version: `git commit hash`
    - OS: `Linux knight 4.4.0-92-generic #115-Ubuntu SMP Thu Aug 10 09:04:33 UTC 2017 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux`
-->
Found during co-simulating rocket-chip with riscv-isa-sim. Page-fault is delegated so rocket-chip goes to S mode while the Spike goes to M mode because of access-fault.
```
   mode different at pc = 0x0000011184, right= 0x0000000000000003, wrong = 0x0000000000000001
mstatus different at pc = 0x0000011184, right= 0x8000000a000060a2, wrong = 0x8000000a000060a8
sstatus different at pc = 0x0000011184, right= 0x8000000200006022, wrong = 0x8000000200006020
   mepc different at pc = 0x0000011184, right= 0x0000000000011186, wrong = 0x000000000001116e
   sepc different at pc = 0x0000011184, right= 0x0000000000010a1a, wrong = 0x0000000000011186
  mtval different at pc = 0x0000011184, right= 0x0000003f9bdf749e, wrong = 0x0000000000000000
  stval different at pc = 0x0000011184, right= 0x0000003f9c07ffac, wrong = 0x0000003f9bdf749e
 mcause different at pc = 0x0000011184, right= 0x0000000000000005, wrong = 0x0000000000000002
 scause different at pc = 0x0000011184, right= 0x000000000000000f, wrong = 0x000000000000000d
```

**What is the use case for changing the behavior?**
Just to align the behavior with Spike and the ISA. I don't think it would be a serious issue for users.

I notice the `pte_addr` is shortened after traversing to the next level. So I think it would be a little bit complicate to fix the behavior by allowing it traverse to the next level. Probably we should just set `ae_ptw` instead in this case.

comments.body:
I tried a fix. This time rocket-chip raises the same access-fault as riscv-isa-sim does.

```
diff --git a/src/main/scala/rocket/PTW.scala b/src/main/scala/rocket/PTW.scala
index 7c36bdbf3..1e0930b77 100644
--- a/src/main/scala/rocket/PTW.scala
+++ b/src/main/scala/rocket/PTW.scala
@@ -720,7 +720,8 @@ class PTW(n: Int)(implicit edge: TLEdgeOut, p: Parameters) extends CoreModule()(
           resp_valid(r_req_dest) := true.B
         }
 
-        resp_ae_final := ae
+        resp_ae_ptw := ae && count <= 1.U && !pte.r && !pte.x
+        resp_ae_final := ae && (count > 1.U || pte.r || pte.x)
         resp_pf := pf && !stage2
         resp_gf := gf || (pf && stage2)
         resp_hr := !stage2 || (!pf && !gf && pte.ur())
```

Please correct me if I'm wrong. If the bug is confirmed, I can submit a PR to fix it.

Probably I'm still missing the condition of reserved bits. Only if the non-leaf PTEs are valid and its PPN refers to an invalid address should we raise access-fault, because accessing the next-level PTE would violate the PMA.

Besides, I found that there may be a separate bug in the page-fault condition in PTW. Currently it checks only the most significant reserved bits (`val pf = pte.v && pte.reserved_for_future =/= 0.U`). However, as discussed in https://github.com/riscv-software-src/riscv-tests/issues/352, non-leaf should not have any of D, A, and U bits set. Therefore, rocket-chip needs to check the D, A, U bits as well for page-fault.

I believe rocket-chip's page-fault condition then would become exactly the same as Spike:
```
if (pte & (PTE_D | PTE_A | PTE_U | PTE_N | PTE_PBMT))
  break;
```

So there would be two separate bugs, for page-fault and access-fault respectively.

The missing cases are:
- access-fault: (1) it is a valid non-leaf PTE; (2) its PPN refers to an invalid address.
- page-fault: a non-leaf PTE has any of D, A, and U bits set.

I've updated two commits to fix the two issues respectively.

- access-fault for non-leaf out-of-range PTE access: https://github.com/poemonsense/rocket-chip/commit/ff025a69dbc9b230de9a2ad386c9b333a92ea46c
```diff
diff --git a/src/main/scala/rocket/PTW.scala b/src/main/scala/rocket/PTW.scala
index 7c36bdbf3..8701caa0b 100644
--- a/src/main/scala/rocket/PTW.scala
+++ b/src/main/scala/rocket/PTW.scala
@@ -720,6 +720,7 @@ class PTW(n: Int)(implicit edge: TLEdgeOut, p: Parameters) extends CoreModule()(
           resp_valid(r_req_dest) := true.B
         }
 
+        resp_ae_ptw := ae && count < (pgLevels-1).U && pte.table()
         resp_ae_final := ae
         resp_pf := pf && !stage2
         resp_gf := gf || (pf && stage2)
```
For non-leaf PTEs (`pte.table()` is set, and `count` is less than the `pgLevels`), we should set `resp_ae_ptw` instead of `resp_ae_final`. Besides, since `resp_ae_final` would have lower priority than page-fault and `ae_ptw` access-fault, we don't need to shrink its condition and keep the condition as simple as possible. 

- page-fault for reserved, non-leaf PTEs: https://github.com/poemonsense/rocket-chip/commit/2a005655d2487fdb0da4e7a526abfff348d2aecb
```diff
diff --git a/src/main/scala/rocket/PTW.scala b/src/main/scala/rocket/PTW.scala
index 8701caa0b..be45281f7 100644
--- a/src/main/scala/rocket/PTW.scala
+++ b/src/main/scala/rocket/PTW.scala
@@ -135,8 +135,12 @@ class PTE(implicit p: Parameters) extends CoreBundle()(p) {
   val r = Bool()
   /** valid bit */
   val v = Bool()
+  /** the most significant bits are reserved for all types of PTE */
+  def isReserved: Bool = reserved_for_future =/= 0.U
+  /** a non-leaf PTE has more reserved bits than the leaf PTEs */
+  def nonLeafIsReserved: Bool = d || a || u
   /** return true if find a pointer to next level page table */
-  def table(dummy: Int = 0) = v && !r && !w && !x && !d && !a && !u && reserved_for_future === 0.U
+  def table(dummy: Int = 0) = v && !r && !w && !x && !isReserved && !nonLeafIsReserved
   /** return true if find a leaf PTE */
   def leaf(dummy: Int = 0) = v && (r || (x && !w)) && a
   /** user read */

comments.body: We can build with VCS versions close to that one, so I think it's probably a configuration issue on your end.  If you have more info, feel free to re-open this, but I think SolvNet might be the right place to get a fix.

I had a similar problem. The relevant Solvnet article suggested that I had conflicting versions of VCS installed, which was not a problem in my case.

The issue for me was that gcc by default uses slightly different linker options on Debian/Ubuntu than on Fedora (which is what VCS is tested on). To fix this it I added -LD_FLAGS -Wl,--no-as-needed to the list of vcs options. That means a full command would look something like

vcs -full64 +v2k top.v -LDFLAGS -Wl,--no-as-needed
For more details on this see this SO post.

**What is the expected behavior?**

Compilation successfully finishes and produces a system with a 256-bit external interface.  Tests can successfully run on the system.

**Please tell us about your environment:**
<!--    (examples)

Would like to increase the external memory interface bit width to provide more memory bandwidth to the system.  Setting the external memory interface bit width with `WithEdgeDataBits` to anything above 128-bits fails due to an issue in AXI4Fragmenter where an index into an address exceeds the overall bit width of the address.  The address index is dependent on beatBytes.  Printing out the slave.maxAddress in the AXI4Fragmenter seems to print addresses corresponding to devices that should not see this change in bit width (debug-controller and interrupt-controller devices).  However, printing out lgBytes shows that they are seeing this bit width change. These devices sit on buses internal to the system where the bit width is unchanged.  The debug-controller specifically is the device that causes the exception since its maxAddress can be represented with only 12-bits.  The shifting of this address by lgBytes produces a resulting bit vector that is too small to be indexed by the AXI len parameter (set to 8).

comments.body:
The problem is not what you explain above.

The problem is that the AXIMMIO simulation memory is only 4kB which is not larger than a full-sized AXI burst with a 256-bit bus.

In src/main/scala/subsystem/Ports.scala, change:
```
-      val mmio_mem = LazyModule(new SimAXIMem(edge, size = 4096))
+      val mmio_mem = LazyModule(new SimAXIMem(edge, size = 4096*2))
```

However, we probably want the AXI4Fragmenter to work also in this case, so I'll fix it instead.

body:
I'm using a design based on the SiFive Freedom E310, and I'm seeing 2 cycles of latency between the Rocket core issuing a data access and it appearing on the tile's TileLink interface.

The subsystem's config had RocketCrossingParams with crossingType = SynchronousCrossing(). I switched to NoCrossing to see if this would reduce the latency, and if so by how much.

It did indeed reduce the latency by 1 cycle each way.

However I then noticed an issue where the DCache would issue a valid pulse whilst the TileLink address bus ready was deasserted, then issue an s2_nack back to the rocket core, but when it replayed the access the address would be incorrect.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1271666/48977757-b12cf480-f0f4-11e8-96d5-a9b864b7eb30.png)


What happened is an offset calculation has been repeated, corrupting the address. My disassembly looks like so:

```
  1c007e:       10050537                lui     a0,0x10050
  1c0082:       0b050513                addi    a0,a0,176 # 100500b0 <spi_load+0xfe9001e>
  1c0086:       f14025f3                csrr    a1,mhartid
  1c008a:       058a                    slli    a1,a1,0x2
  1c008c:       95aa                    add     a1,a1,a0
  1c008e:       4188                    lw      a0,0(a1)
  1c0090:       8502                    jr      a0
```

The issue is that the ```add a1,a1,a0``` occurs again (the core executes and completes the instruction at 0x1c008c a second time), resulting in an incorrect address in a1.

I've often wondered why the rocket core seems to replay instead of stalling while the various hazards or buses clear. Anyway, does this look like a real bug, and not a configuration issue? Is rocket supposed to work with NoCrossing?

fix_commits.messageHeadline: Make sure there's at least one TL.A register in the NoCrossing case

comments.body: I'm not able to replicate this.  I wrote some identical code, except with different absolute addresses, but with the same code alignment; and I made it so that the first time the `lw` executes, `a.ready` is false, so the nack occurs.  After the pipeline flush, the program resumes executing at the `lw`, as expected; the `add` instruction is not repeated.
If you can send me your waveform, I can perhaps try to understand what's going on.

Thanks for looking into this.

Our design has moved on a little bit since I filed the issue and I haven't been able to recreate the failure.

We are using some custom instruction fetch logic, and I can't rule out the bug being there. I thought I checked it at the time but I didn't store the waveform and I have fixed bugs in the frontend since I filed this. So this is likely a false alarm, sorry about that.

However, I do have an observation about a new issue I now see with the NoCrossing configuration. In trying to recreate this scenario, I configured 4 rocket harts with crossingType=NoCrossing again, and re-run our software. I then noticed the software wasn't progressing and noticed a deadlock of sorts. There is a semaphore register that 3 cores are attempting to claim (atomic swap instruction) and one core trying to release it by writing zero. The system becomes deadlocked because the hart trying to clear the register happens to see a deasserted ready from the tilelink bus every time it attempts the write.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1271666/49697107-7607e680-fc07-11e8-8883-88af7ca90074.png)

I notice when we do have SynchronousCrossing set, the valid out from the tile is held until ready is asserted and the transaction is acked by the bus.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1271666/49697121-a8194880-fc07-11e8-9945-8f66e997866c.png)

I guess the only way to get this behaviour is with SynchronousCrossing? I presume it'd take changes in the dcache to change the behaviour with NoCrossing?

Thanks again for looking into this. If I do see anything like this in future I'll be sure to save the trace.
Thanks for the update on the previous issue.

Is `SynchronousCrossing(BufferParams.flow)` appropriate for your use case?  This will prevent the livelock issue you observed, but retain the lower latency.

If so, then I think the right thing to do is to add a requirement to the D$ to ban the `NoCrossing` a.k.a. `SynchronousCrossing(BufferParams.none)` case.  I suspect the D$ is not the only component that makes this assumption, but it is a start.  @hcook sound ok?

Nice one, will give this  ago but I reckon it looks good.

Thanks @aswaterman !

title: PMA is not working in Rocket Core
body:
<!-- THIS REPOSITORY'S ISSUES ARE RESERVED FOR FEATURE REQUESTS AND BUG REPORTS. -->
<!-- For support questions related to Rocket Chip, please use [Stack Overflow [rocket-chip]](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/rocket-chip). -->
<!-- For support questions related to Chisel, please use [Stack Overflow [chisel]](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/chisel). -->
<!-- Please select the item best describing the issue in each category and delete the other items. -->

<!-- choose all that apply -->
**Type of issue**: bug report

<!-- choose one -->
**Impact**: unknown

<!-- choose one -->
**Development Phase**: request

**Other information**

In `rocket/DCache.sv`, `pma_checker` is connected as follows (https://github.com/chipsalliance/rocket-chip/blob/master/src/main/scala/rocket/DCache.scala#L269):

```scala
pma_checker.io <> DontCare
pma_checker.io.req.bits.passthrough := true.B
pma_checker.io.req.bits <> s1_req
```

This connection seems to miss out most fields in TLBReq. Crucially, `vaddr` is not connected.

Currently the only usage of pma_checker's response is to set `s2_pma` when TLB is not ready, which is possible in some cases (e.g. if the type of memory operation is prefetch or fence). It seems to me that prefetches are not handled in DCache right now, and IIRC individual fences are not affected by PMAs? So the `pma_checker` code path is mostly redundant? If that's the case, can we remove them all together? If that's not the case, then this may be a bug.

This is found during the effort to convert rocket-chip to chisel3 (#3110), which changed the bi-directional connection semantic to disallowing missing fields in either side of the connection.

comments.body:
> So the `pma_checker` code path is mostly redundant?

To fully understand the `pma_checker` we have to go back to the commit ["Expose DTLB access port"](https://github.com/chipsalliance/rocket-chip/pull/2270/commits/dc68c21e8e5662c81fba003a7579123735c757ef) which introduced this module.

In that commit, a `tlb_port` IO was added to `DCache`, and `DCache` has to handle requests from both `cpu` and `tlb_port`. In cases when we only have requests from one of them, requests are handled through `tlb` and everything is fine.

However, when we have requests from both of them, things become tricky. the author allowed one certain case: when the request from cpu is a physical address and has no exception. In all other cases, request from cpu is nacked.

https://github.com/chipsalliance/rocket-chip/blob/70ed8b63bd3780b2c6091a9e9fbfd12ab9145200/src/main/scala/rocket/DCache.scala#L265 

For that specific case, `pma_checker`, which is an extra TLB, only uses the PMPChecker part (that's why passthrough is always asserted true.B) and handles the request from cpu.

However, the author did not connect the request properly. `s1_req` is not of type `TLBReq` and has no `vaddr` field and should be manually connected in the following way instead of a bulk connection; but, Chisel2 allowed such connection and did not care about the unconnected port.

```chisel
  pma_checker.io.req.bits.vaddr := s1_req.addr
  pma_checker.io.req.bits.size := s1_req.size
  pma_checker.io.req.bits.cmd := s1_req.cmd
  // extra field from later commits
  pma_checker.io.req.bits.prv := s1_req.dprv
  pma_checker.io.req.bits.v := s1_req.dv
```

Fortunately, rocket-chip itself never used the extra `tlb_port` and is not affected. So the title should be changed to "PMA is not working in Rocket Core DCache when there are requests from cpu and tlb_port"
It spends me about 3 hours to think how to test this... And still have no idea on it.(Maybe eventually we need unittests to verify those uarch behavior???)

On Tue, Oct 03, 2023 at 03:50:21AM -0700, Norbert Kremeris wrote:
> @gsomlo
> You can download firtool from here

Oh, great! First mill, OK. Now some other rando download -- this is
quickly headed for NPM-like levels of dependency hell... :(

> Oh, great! First mill, OK. Now some other rando download -- this is
> quickly headed for NPM-like levels of dependency hell... :(

😂 That's not just any rando dependency. 😂  That's a much more (~4x conservatively) performant FIRRTL compiler that produces better, more readable Verilog output. 😉 

Note that on the Chisel side, we are intending to make this download automatically handled like a normal Java dependency. @jackkoenig has an experimental approach that will download this for you from Maven. It's slightly more complicated than normal as it's a binary dependency and not a Java dependency and this has taken some time to sort out.

In order to resolve the dependency issues(and avoid NPM dependency hell as well), In rocket-chip, I choose these solutions:
- for JVM stack-software, use mill for build and dependency management(believe me SBT sucks);
- for dependencies that don't provide a release, use mill to build from source: hardfloat, cde, riscv-opcodes
- for native dependencies, we use nix to manage them, and make it be able to run in different architecture and distros, (e.g. most user use x86, while I'm using an aarch64-linux, some use Ubuntu, while I'm using Arch). for native dependencies, there are two different parts:
1. software for elaboration and emulation, e.g. circt, espresso, verilator.
2. software for test case generation, e.g. riscv-gcc riscv-clang, riscv arch test, riscv tests.

I understand installing nix, and run a daemon for it is not quite straightforward for hardware design users, I aware that, and I'll also try to find some alternative solutions to new users(e.g. provide a docker container and release it)

I hope users understand, we reduces burdens(SBT, legacy Chisel version support, a stable API and a version based backport-flow) since
1. dependencies are hard to manage, there are different ways to manage, see other project from Google, they even depend on a shared cache. Nix may be hard to understand by new users, but it really save our time.
2. build system are hard to manage, mill does have some shortages(e.g. absolute path), but it's almost a state of the art comparing to other different build systems.(SiFive even develop their own build system https://github.com/sifive/wake)
3. We have a limited human resource to manage such a big project. For now only 2 active PhD(I and Jerry) are maintaining it(originally the entire SiFive R&D)

After all, we are still making progress, we may have some breaking change, or even introduce issues that makes some user not happy(like this) in the future, but please understand, our goal  for now is improving the development efficiency to make the rocket-chip continue and alive at least.

So for most dependencies/build questions, my only suggestion is:
`nix develop -c mill resolve __` and read the build script to see what you can do.

> @sequencer Is it possible to have mill parse a string for the Config as it was done before? Having to mirror the configs into the build.sc is not ideal

It's not simple, since, mill find configuration statically, there are two solutions:
1. provide these configuration from another file, e.g. "config.json", and mill read this file to generate the task graph.(See what I did in chipsalliance/t1 ;p)
2. parse Scala Config, and automatically generate the task via meta-build feature, which is not a trivial work, and I think we don't have bandwidth for it.

On Tue, Oct 03, 2023 at 02:57:05PM -0700, Jiuyang Liu wrote:
> In order to resolve the dependency issues(and avoid NPM dependency hell as
> well), In rocket-chip, I choose these solutions:

@sequencer, @jerryz123: First off, thank you for your hard work
maintaining this project. Last thing I want is to add "negative energy"
from the peanut gallery, and sorry if anything I said reads that way... :)

As a "downstream consumer" of RocketChip, I (personally) value the
ability to trust the output of a build process by keeping a handle
on all (most?) of the "moving parts". A large part of that is ability
to understand, track, and control the "main" project's dependencies.

It makes sense for a project such as Rocket to depend on a few other
projects that are also "fast-evolving" in their own right (e.g.,
Chisel, mill, etc.).

But in order to maintain any sort of confidence in the output of a
build of the project, as we descend down the tree of dependencies, things
should hopefully settle down into "slow-and-stable", i.e. things that
might be reasonably packaged for a distro (debian/ubuntu/fedora/etc.)
and updated once every few months, if not even less frequently.

If the "fast-evolving" nature of the dependency chain is preserved too
many layers deep, then we have an "everything everywhere all at once"
situation that only one or two developers can reasonably keep a handle
on, and anyone else might get lucky to receive a dockerfile of a snapshot
of one of the developers' environments, so as to be able to ritually
"cargo-cult" a rebuild, but without any chance of any control or
understanding of what's going on.

I understand the latter scenario is sometimes inevitable, and that's
OK, I'm happy to wait for it to stabilize once again. I wish I were
enough of a Chisel/Scala ninja to offer some assistance, but that's
not (yet) the case... :(

Best of luck with your degrees, that should be priority #1! :D

Cheers,
--Gabriel

comments.body:
This is because there's no "%" in the list of targets of this recipe.  A non-pattern recipe with multiple targets is actually just multiple recipes, so this is directly telling make to run Chisel three times.  You'll probably also see this fall over and die on parallel builds.

The easiest way to fix it is probably to just have a Chisel stamp, but finding a way to massage this into a pattern-based recipe would also fix the problem.
I believe I've fixed this in the Chisel 3 Makefile, so I'm going to close the issue since the old version will eventually go away.
Good enough for me!

title: FIRRTL Bump breaks code in JTAG Tap
body:
The currently submoduled version of Chisel/FIRRTL breaks the JTAG TAP controller (which is ~~one of the few~~ the only modules in the codebase written in chisel3._ . It blows away the `irReg` due to the way it interprets something in the JtagTapController and/or DebugTransportModuleJTAG.

In the "pre-bump" Chisel, there is a line in `DebugTransportModuleJTAG` FIRRTL output:
```
JtagTapController.io is invalid
```

That line is not present in the new version. It's not SUPPOSED to have to be present. But it seems to blow things away as a result in the output Verilog. And there is no complaint. Will file a relevant bug on FIRRTL as well. If this line is manually added to the FIRRTL, then things work as expected.

Note that reverting to `Chisel._` works as a fix.

FYI @ducky64

title: Issue with DIV result not being written back to register file
body:
<!-- THIS REPOSITORY'S ISSUES ARE RESERVED FOR FEATURE REQUESTS AND BUG REPORTS. -->
<!-- For support questions related to Rocket Chip, please use [Stack Overflow [rocket-chip]](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/rocket-chip). -->
<!-- For support questions related to Chisel, please use [Stack Overflow [chisel]](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/chisel). -->
<!-- Please select the item best describing the issue in each category and delete the other items. -->

<!-- choose all that apply -->
**Type of issue**: bug report

**Other information**
On a Rocket core, I encountered the issue that the although the core accepts the result of the div (div.io_resp_valid & div.io_resp_ready), the data picked for the register file update (rf_wdata) is actually the dmem data. How did the core reach that situation? There is a memory instruction in the writeback state in that cycle that caught a npc_misaligned in the memory stage - so it turns to an exception in WB, allowing the div to write back its result by giving the div.io_resp_ready, but since the npc_misaligned case does not cause the activation of io_dmem_s1_kill, the dcache is free to actually give a response for this memory instruction, in particular, in case of a cache hit, the one that is causing the mux for rf_write to pick the dcache output instead of the div one.
I am attaching a waveform from a Scala-generated RTL. Please ignore the "ILLEGAL" text in the line otherwise showing the instruction - this is a debug signal from out verification environment that currently does not take the full instruction set into account.
Of course, this is on the Rocket level, not a full RocketTile. So can the Frontend deliver a misaligned PC like in this case? In general, it can - I have a configuration where misa is writeable, so take a write to clear the 'c' bit in misa followed by setting bit 1 in tvec followed by an instruction causing an exception. This requests the misaligned PC from tvec at the Frontend which it happily delivers, causing a situation where a non-CFI instruction causes a npc misaligned which is actually a "current PC misaligned".

![npc_misaligned](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/45827187/49926841-d1aeca00-febc-11e8-9922-a0b1ffd194d1.png)

fix_commits.messageHeadline: Move tvec bit-zapping from D to Q
Move tvec bit-zapping from D to Q
Move tvec bit-zapping from D to Q
Move tvec bit-zapping from D to Q
Move tvec bit-zapping from D to Q

comments.body:
I'm pretty sure something you're doing is violating an implicit property of one of the interfaces.  mem_npc_misaligned should only ever be high for CFIs.

tvec bit 1 is hardwired to 0, so taking an exception can't result in the PC being misaligned.

Well, the attached trace was produced on the RocketTile - it takes some writes to CSRs to disable compressed instructions and then get to the situation where an address ending in ee is requested (value at the cursor position). So it seems in principle, the frontent can deliver misaligned PCs (this was obtained with formal verification - other traces could likely be found as well, this was just the shortest one).
![npc_misaligned_tile](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/45827187/50272330-bb15ef00-0437-11e9-8a17-fc504fa06b4e.png)
I currently do not have a trace where this occurs together with the DIV (getting a cache hit takes more cycles I guess). I just say that in the case that the frontend delivers a misaligned PC, external units like mem are not properly cancelled if requested which may cause issues like the DIV I reported. Form an architecture point of view, it may make sense to have the core also cancel the external requests in mem stage for misaligned - so in the case that is unexpected in the overall system (pc misaligned), the core "just" causes the npc_misaligned, but no other side effects...
Can you please provide the code sequence that corresponds to the waveform?

I am not trying this on software - just on the RTL. But I can extract the sequence of data words provided by the frontend from the simulation trace...
So I see 30199573 followed (CSR update of 301) by 3a082073 (CSR update of 3a0) and 10200073 (CSR update of 102). The next one then is the exception one: 100073 (a break?). The initial register values in the register file were picked as 0. And the initial PC (as it is an input of the RocketTile) was picked as 7ffffff8 (so just 31 bits used, not 38 like in the other issue). The instruction hitting the exception requests 657bcfee as PC.
This is on the RocketTile, so the Frontend is in the model as well.
Can you just send me the waveform? Talking about this over github isn't working.

Thanks for sending the waveform.  I see that stvec[1] is set.  The privileged ISA forbids this; stvec[1] is always supposed to be 0.

It's a situation where the simulation model is more pessimistic than the synthesized result.  The only data source to the stvec register has its bit 1 wired to 0.  (You'll observe this if you try write stvec: stvec[1] will become 0, no matter what you write to it.)  Synthesis will optimize the flop into a constant 0.

That said, there's no reason to have this mismatch.  I'll make a patch to make the RTL simulation better behaved.
I can confirm that the PC no longer gets misaligned, solving the reported DIV issue.

title: phy/ecp5rgmii: Incorrect parameters in DELAYF blocks
body:
In some recent debugging I've discovered that nextpnr does not consider strings such as `"DELAY80"` a valid parameter value for `DEL_VALUE` 

See in this snippet, taken from the ecp5rgmii phy

```python
rx_delay_taps = 80

self.specials += [
       Instance("DELAYF",
                p_DEL_MODE  = "SCLK_ALIGNED",
                p_DEL_VALUE = "DELAY{}".format(rx_delay_taps),
                i_LOADN     = 1,
                i_MOVE      = 0,
                i_DIRECTION = 0,
                i_A         = pads.rx_ctl,
                o_Z         = rx_ctl_delayf),
]
```

This results in a design where all the IO_DELAY blocks are set to the same value. 
(The value set is actually 50 rather than 0 because of the `SCLK_ALIGNED` mode see nextpnr code [here](https://github.com/YosysHQ/nextpnr/blob/576baa994f4b9e1746a231469bfd9e65d1d5a2b4/ecp5/pack.cc#L1981) )

This creates a design that sometimes runs, but sometimes does not run because the timing is very marginal.

title: Litex SoC binds to non-existent ports when generating a NaxRiscv-based SoC with --with-jtag-instruction
body:
Hello,

# Issue
I'm trying to implement a NaxRiscv-based SoC on FPGA (Digilent Genesys 2) but synthesis fails, as the SoC's top level module instantiating the Nax tries to connect to port which do not exist.

Precisely, I'm trying to add a JTAG debug module within the Nax, which thus exposes I/O ports in the Nax's top level. For some reason, when integrating the Nax in the SoC's top level, Litex seems to detect different signal names for the JTAG ports, than the ones actually exposed by the Nax, which thus causes an error during synthesis.


Instantation of the NaxRiscv in the SoC top module (namely the verilog file ```build/gateware/digilent_genesys2.v```)
```verilog
//------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Instance NaxRiscvLitex_ac66cf5e80a0da4a2f58fc5f9f240934 of NaxRiscvLitex_ac66cf5e80a0da4a2f58fc5f9f240934 Module.
//------------------------------------------------------------------------------
NaxRiscvLitex_ac66cf5e80a0da4a2f58fc5f9f240934 NaxRiscvLitex_ac66cf5e80a0da4a2f58fc5f9f240934(
        /* Remaining ports connections */
        .jtag_instruction_capture           (basesoc_jtag_capture),
        .jtag_instruction_clk               (basesoc_jtag_clk),
        .jtag_instruction_enable            (basesoc_jtag_enable),
        .jtag_instruction_reset             (basesoc_jtag_reset),
        .jtag_instruction_shift             (basesoc_jtag_shift),
        .jtag_instruction_tdi               (basesoc_jtag_tdi),
        .jtag_instruction_update            (basesoc_jtag_update),
        /* Remaining ports connections */
       	);
```

Definition of the NaxRiscv top module
```verilog
module NaxRiscvLitex_ac66cf5e80a0da4a2f58fc5f9f240934 (
	/* Remaining ports declaration */
	input  wire          jtag_instruction_instruction_tdi,
	input  wire          jtag_instruction_instruction_enable,
	input  wire          jtag_instruction_instruction_capture,
	input  wire          jtag_instruction_instruction_shift,
	input  wire          jtag_instruction_instruction_update,
	input  wire          jtag_instruction_instruction_reset,
	output wire          jtag_instruction_instruction_tdo,
	input  wire          jtag_instruction_clk
	/* Remaining ports declaration */
);
	/* RTL */
endmodule
```

As one can see from the above RTL snippets, except for ```jtag_instruction_clk``` which is correct, JTAG signals are declared with prefix ```jtag_instruction_instruction``` whilst the SoC is mapping to ports with prefix ```jtag_instruction```.

# Build options

Here are my build options to try and recreate the issue :
```bash
python3 -m litex_boards.targets.digilent_genesys2.py \
--cpu-type=naxriscv \
--toolchain=vivado \
--build \
--bios-console=lite --bios-format=double \
--synth-mode=vivado \
--bus-standard=wishbone --bus-data-width=32 --bus-address-width=32 --bus-interconnect=crossbar \
--watchdog-width=32 \
--uart-name=serial --uart-baudrate=921600 --uart-fifo-depth=16 \
--l2-size=1024 --integrated-rom-size=131072 --integrated-sram-size=16536 --integrated-main-ram-size=0 \
--sys-clk-freq=200000000.0 \
--no-netlist-cache --update-repo=latest \
--cpu-variant=standard --xlen=32 --cpu-count=1 \
--l2-bytes=131072 --l2-ways=8 --with-rvc --with-fpu --with-coherent-dma \
--with-jtag-instruction
```

Actually, I use a modified version of ```litex_boards.targets.digilent_genesys2``` in which I added  the following lines (right-after the ```BaseSoc``` instantiation in ```main()```) :

```python
from litex.soc.cores.jtag import XilinxJTAG
soc.jtag = jtag = XilinxJTAG(XilinxJTAG.get_primitive(soc.platform.device), chain=4)
soc.comb += [
    soc.cpu.jtag_reset.eq(jtag.reset),
    soc.cpu.jtag_capture.eq(jtag.capture),
    soc.cpu.jtag_shift.eq(jtag.shift),
    soc.cpu.jtag_update.eq(jtag.update),
    soc.cpu.jtag_clk.eq(jtag.tck),
    soc.cpu.jtag_tdi.eq(jtag.tdi),
    soc.cpu.jtag_enable.eq(True),
    jtag.tdo.eq(soc.cpu.jtag_tdo),
]
```

Note: I added the latter modifications following this tutorial from Litex Wiki [JTAG GDB Debugging with VexRiscv SMP NaxRiscv VexiiRiscv CPUs](https://github.com/enjoy-digital/litex/wiki/JTAG-GDB-Debugging-with-VexRiscv-SMP-NaxRiscv-VexiiRiscv-CPUs#debugging-on-physical-hardware-directly-though-bscane2-jtag-primitive), as I would like to route the JTAG module to the FPGA's built-in JTAG.

# Question

I was wondering if anyone knows why Litex catches wrong names specifically for these signals ? Also, perhaps, is there a way to force the name of these ```XilinxJTAG``` signals to have prefix ```jtag_instruction``` instead of ```jtag_instruction_instruction``` ?

Thanks,
Regards,

comments.body:
Hello @benjaminh-13,

I suggest 2 solutions: 

- either make a modification on the NaxRiscv side, 
- or make a modification on the Litex side.

#### On the NaxRiscv side

You'll need to modify the file that generates the SoC for Litex, NaxSoc, by changing this line :

https://github.com/SpinalHDL/NaxRiscv/blob/43716b5770e8ac689e9778056c061da577dcf17e/src/main/scala/naxriscv/platform/litex/NaxSoc.scala#L209

by this one : 

```scala
if (withJtagInstruction) debug.instruction.setName("jtag")
```

What happens is that the string `jtag_instruction` is added to the variable name `instruction` in [DebugModuleFiber](https://github.com/SpinalHDL/SpinalHDL/blob/af8fab4da5a73c785c4f2e2f68af2c9b34fd6aec/lib/src/main/scala/spinal/lib/cpu/riscv/debug/DebugModuleFiber.scala#L95) when the verilog is generated.

So to change the name of the totality, another way would be as follows :

```scala
if (withJtagInstruction) debug.instruction.instruction.setName("jtag_instruction")
```

#### On the Litex side

You need to modify the core.py file associated with NaxRiscv.

https://github.com/enjoy-digital/litex/blob/48e65c199de6bd1d5aead61d7f515356cc7ecab8/litex/soc/cores/cpu/naxriscv/core.py#L428-L437

You need to update the assignments with the “jtag_instruction_instruction” prefix.

```python
self.cpu_params.update(
    i_jtag_instruction_clk     = self.jtag_clk,
    i_jtag_instruction_instruction_enable  = self.jtag_enable,
    i_jtag_instruction_instruction_capture = self.jtag_capture,
    i_jtag_instruction_instruction_shift   = self.jtag_shift,
    i_jtag_instruction_instruction_update  = self.jtag_update,
    i_jtag_instruction_instruction_reset   = self.jtag_reset,
    i_jtag_instruction_instruction_tdi     = self.jtag_tdi,
    o_jtag_instruction_instruction_tdo     = self.jtag_tdo,
)
```

After one of these two modifications, the Vivado synthesis should work.

Best regards

Hello @atkarim,

Thank you for the very quick response.

I tried solution 2, namely bringing changes to the NaxRiscv's ```core.py``` in Litex and now synthesis succeeds. As a consequence, I am closing this issue.

Thanks again,
Best regards,

title: Endianness in WishboneDMAReader
body:
Hi,

Shouldn't this be opposite ? 
https://github.com/enjoy-digital/litex/blob/78c1751c4781ffe156128748810ee4af85fee058/litex/soc/cores/dma.py#L19-L20

Just to try this out I used the `WishboneDMAReader` in a module of my SoC (with vexriscv) simulation to read a word from SRAM and print it in my C code and it printed reversed. The complete system is little endian.
```
DMA Read from : 0x10003fac
Readback from DMA: 0xdf0feca
Actual value : 0xcafef00d
```

with the format_bytes reversed
```python
 def format_bytes(s, endianness): 
     return {"little": s, "big": reverse_bytes(s)}[endianness]
```
the print is as expected

```
DMA Read from : 0x10003fac
Readback from DMA: 0xcafef00d
Actual value : 0xcafef00d
```

comments.body:
Hi @navaneeth-cirel,

this probably similar to https://github.com/enjoy-digital/litedram/issues/251. There is a endianness mismatch between the model and real hardware. I'll try to address this soon.

Hi @enjoy-digital ,

After brief look at the issue referenced it seems that there is a mismatch between the simulation and target hardware, but in my case I am seeing the mismatch in Simulation itself.
Just to give more clarity , what I am doing is writing a 32bit value to a `uint32_t` variable in the C code and set its address to the DMA to read and transfer to a CSR status register which I am then reading and printing in the C code, where the mismatch is observed.

I re-checked the current code and your observation still makes sense for a direct word-level use of `WishboneDMAReader`.

For a little-endian CPU writing `0xcafef00d` as a `uint32_t`, the Wishbone word read back by the DMA is already `0xcafef00d`. Passing `endianness="little"` to `WishboneDMAReader` then applies `reverse_bytes()`, so a direct word consumer such as a CSR status register will see `0x0df0feca`.

So for raw word-oriented use, the DMA should be instantiated with `endianness="big"` / no byte swap.

I would avoid flipping the global `format_bytes()` mapping since the DMA is also used in byte-stream storage paths, where this conversion is part of the expected byte ordering. The real issue is that the parameter is confusing for direct word users, so we should probably document this better and/or add a clearer no-swap/raw mode in the future.

This has now been improved with:  c4baeb3e1a3a35ecaa3e47eae4d2951b64d76bdd

The existing DMA endianness behavior is kept for compatibility: `endianness="little"` still byte-swaps and `endianness="big"` still preserves the raw Wishbone word.

To make direct word-oriented use cases clearer, `WishboneDMAReader` and `WishboneDMAWriter` now also have an explicit `with_byteswap` override. So for a raw word transfer such as the `0xcafef00d` case discussed here, the DMA can now be instantiated with:

```python
  WishboneDMAReader(bus, endianness="little", with_byteswap=False)
```

This preserves the raw Wishbone word instead of byte-swapping it.

I also added regression coverage for the reported word-level case on both reader and writer, checking both the legacy little-endian byte-swap behavior and the explicit no-swap path.

I also added a follow-up test commit to double-check the default behavior: https://github.com/enjoy-digital/litex/commit/db2678d1a2df8f47c76510fec134c4a093cf45cc

This adds regression coverage for the storage-style byte-stream path used by LiteSDCard/LiteSATA, where DMA words are converted to/from 8-bit streams with reverse stream converters.

The tests confirm why the legacy default remains unchanged for these users, while raw word-oriented users can use the explicit `with_byteswap=False` override added above.

With the explicit `with_byteswap=False` override and the added regression tests for both raw word and byte-stream DMA paths, I think this is now covered. Closing, but please reopen or open a follow-up if another DMA endianness case still behaves unexpectedly.

comments.body: Removing `-flto` [here](https://github.com/enjoy-digital/litex/blob/master/litex/soc/software/common.mak#L56) seems to be the intermediate fix for the demo to work on Rocket.

While this does work it also breaks some other stuff.
The real issue is that the version of the toolchain that you and I were using is broken.
Update your toolchain to a more recent on like [this](https://github.com/riscv-collab/riscv-gnu-toolchain/releases/tag/2022.03.09) and it should work again.
Thanks @developandplay, we can now probably close this issue. @Aravindh-Swaminathan: If you still have troubles, please re-open.

Hi @developandplay ,
I tried your solutions in the following order. 
1) Updated the riscv-gnu-toolchain to the latest one (for ubuntu 20.04 version) and checked. The demo application code did not run after Liftoff
2) Removed the -flto flag from common.mak file and tried again. The demo application code runs perfectly fine. 

From this we can say riscv-gnu-toolchain might not be the issue. Kindly advise. 

Thanks.

Did you compile both the BIOS and the demo application code with the new toolchain?
For me it would only work if both of them use the latest toolchain.

@developandplay Yes! I did compile both BIOS and demo application using latest toolchain only since I did not want to leave anything to chance. Still did not work . However, I will try that once again and post back here if there is any change.

Hi @developandplay ,
I have reverified from my end. 
- Made sure to use latest toolchain
- added -flto flag in the common.mak file 
- compiled both BIOS and demo.bin - **Application did not run after Liftoff**
- subsequently removed the -flto flag and recompiled BIOS and demo.bin - **Application works successfully after Liftoff without any issues**

Hi @developandplay ,
Checked with #1259 as per your suggestion and it works perfectly fine.
Thanks!

This should now be covered by current LiteX.

The two build issues from the original report were fixed with enjoy-digital/litex@884ee45c289e1a1650937355c6356b3f64ee0c3a: Rocket now uses `-mcmodel=medany`, and the ISR/PIC initialization code is shared so the demo no longer misses `plic_init`.

The runtime issue after `Liftoff!` was also related to LTO. LTO is no longer enabled by default since enjoy-digital/litex@3ab7eaa5f7afb4d432b5641d7761813d3274d25f, and is now opt-in with enjoy-digital/litex@b9a1fec30fd1f0691f9c6463bac24ea1da75355a.

So the default `demo.bin` build should no longer hit this Rocket issue. I think this can be closed. If a Rocket demo failure still reproduces on current LiteX, please reopen/provide a fresh reproducer, especially noting whether LTO was explicitly enabled.

set_property -dict {PACKAGE_PIN V14 IOSTANDARD LVCMOS33} [get_ports {vga_vsync}];
"""
# CRG ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

class _CRG(Module):
    def __init__(self, platform, sys_clk_freq, with_rst=True):
        self.rst = Signal()
        self.clock_domains.cd_sys       = ClockDomain()
        self.clock_domains.cd_sys4x     = ClockDomain(reset_less=True)
        self.clock_domains.cd_sys4x_dqs = ClockDomain(reset_less=True)
        self.clock_domains.cd_idelay    = ClockDomain()
        self.clock_domains.cd_eth       = ClockDomain()
        self.clock_domains.cd_vga       = ClockDomain(reset_less=True)

        # # #

        self.submodules.pll = pll = S7PLL(speedgrade=-1)
        rst    = ~platform.request("cpu_reset") if with_rst else 0
        self.comb += pll.reset.eq(rst | self.rst)
        pll.register_clkin(platform.request("clk100"), 100e6)
        pll.create_clkout(self.cd_sys,       sys_clk_freq)
        pll.create_clkout(self.cd_sys4x,     4*sys_clk_freq)
        pll.create_clkout(self.cd_sys4x_dqs, 4*sys_clk_freq, phase=90)
        pll.create_clkout(self.cd_idelay,    200e6)
        pll.create_clkout(self.cd_eth,       25e6)
        pll.create_clkout(self.cd_vga, 25e6, margin=1e-3)
        platform.add_false_path_constraints(self.cd_sys.clk, pll.clkin) # Ignore sys_clk to pll.clkin path created by SoC's rst.

        self.submodules.idelayctrl = S7IDELAYCTRL(self.cd_idelay)

        self.comb += platform.request("eth_ref_clk").eq(self.cd_eth.clk)

# BaseSoC ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

class BaseSoC(SoCCore):
    def __init__(self, variant="a7-35", toolchain="vivado", sys_clk_freq=int(100e6), with_ethernet=False, with_etherbone=False, eth_ip="192.168.1.50", eth_dynamic_ip=False, with_jtagbone=True, with_mapped_flash=False, with_spi_flash = False,
        with_pmod_gpio = False, with_led_chaser = True, **kwargs):
        platform = arty.Platform(variant=variant, toolchain=toolchain)


        # SoCCore ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
        SoCCore.__init__(self, platform, sys_clk_freq, **kwargs)

        # CRG --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
        self.submodules.crg = _CRG(platform, sys_clk_freq, False) #, with_mapped_flash)

        # DDR3 SDRAM -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
        if not self.integrated_main_ram_size:
            self.submodules.ddrphy = s7ddrphy.A7DDRPHY(platform.request("ddram"),
                memtype        = "DDR3",
                nphases        = 4,
                sys_clk_freq   = sys_clk_freq)
            self.add_sdram("sdram",
                phy           = self.ddrphy,
                module        = MT41K128M16(sys_clk_freq, "1:4"),
                l2_cache_size = kwargs.get("l2_size", 8192)
            )

        # Ethernet / Etherbone ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        if with_ethernet or with_etherbone:
            self.submodules.ethphy = LiteEthPHYMII(
                clock_pads = self.platform.request("eth_clocks"),
                pads       = self.platform.request("eth"))
            if with_ethernet:
                self.add_ethernet(phy=self.ethphy, dynamic_ip=eth_dynamic_ip)
            if with_etherbone:
                self.add_etherbone(phy=self.ethphy, ip_address=eth_ip)

        # Jtagbone ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
        if with_jtagbone:
            self.add_jtagbone()

        # Flash (through LiteSPI, experimental).
        if with_mapped_flash:
            self.submodules.spiflash_phy  = LiteSPIPHY(platform.request("spiflash4x"), S25FL128L(Codes.READ_1_1_4))
            self.submodules.spiflash_mmap = LiteSPI(self.spiflash_phy, clk_freq=sys_clk_freq, mmap_endianness=self.cpu.endianness)
            spiflash_region = SoCRegion(origin=self.mem_map.get("spiflash", None), size=S25FL128L.total_size, cached=False)
            self.bus.add_slave(name="spiflash", slave=self.spiflash_mmap.bus, region=spiflash_region)

        # SPI Flash --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
        if with_spi_flash:
            from litespi.modules import S25FL128L
            from litespi.opcodes import SpiNorFlashOpCodes as Codes
            self.add_spi_flash(mode="4x", module=S25FL128L(Codes.READ_1_1_4), with_master=True)

        # Leds -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
        if with_led_chaser:
            self.submodules.leds = LedChaser(
                pads         = platform.request_all("user_led"),
                sys_clk_freq = sys_clk_freq)

        # GPIOs ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
        if with_pmod_gpio:
            platform.add_extension(arty.raw_pmod_io("pmoda"))
            self.submodules.gpio = GPIOTristate(platform.request("pmoda"))

        """
        if with_spi:
            #SPI pins and GPIO pins cannot be the same
            platform.add_extension([("spi0", 0,
                #Subsignal("cs_n", Pins("A3")), #A3=JP1:6
                #Subsignal("clk",  Pins("D3")), #D3=JP1:2
                #Subsignal("mosi", Pins("C3")), #C3=JP1:4
                #Subsignal("miso", Pins("A2")), #A2=JP1:5
                Subsignal("cs_n", Pins("A10")), #A10=ADC CS
                Subsignal("clk",  Pins("B14")), #B14=ADC CLK
                Subsignal("mosi", Pins("B10")), #B10=ADC SADDR
                Subsignal("miso", Pins("A9")),  # A9=ADC SDAT
                IOStandard("3.3-V LVTTL"))])

            self.add_spi_port(name="spi0");
        """

            from litex.build.generic_platform import Pins, IOStandard, Subsignal
            platform.add_extension([("vga", 0, #PMOD VGA on pmod B & C
                Subsignal("hsync", Pins("U14")), #pmodc.4
                Subsignal("vsync", Pins("V14")), #pmodc.5
                Subsignal("r", Pins("E15 E16 D15 C15")), #pmodb.0-3
                Subsignal("g", Pins("U12 V12 V10 V11")), #pmodc.0-3
                Subsignal("b", Pins("J17 J18 K15 J15")), #pmodb.4-7
                IOStandard("LVCMOS33"))])

            from litex.soc.cores.video import VideoVGAPHY
            self.submodules.videophy = VideoVGAPHY(platform.request("vga"), clock_domain="vga")
            self.add_video_framebuffer(phy=self.videophy, timings="640x480@60Hz", clock_domain="vga", format="rgb565")


        #DMA
        with_dma = True
        if with_dma:
            from litex.soc.cores.dma import WishboneDMAReader
            from litex.soc.interconnect import wishbone
            dma_width = 32 #FIXME read memory width
            self.submodules.dma_reader = WishboneDMAReader(endianness="big", bus=wishbone.Interface(data_width=dma_width), with_csr=True)
            self.bus.add_master("dma_reader", self.dma_reader.bus)
            if True: #needed in Arty
                from litex.soc.cores.dma import WishboneDMAWriter
                self.submodules.dma_writer = WishboneDMAWriter(endianness="big", bus=wishbone.Interface(data_width=dma_width), with_csr=True)
                self.bus.add_master("dma_writer", self.dma_writer.bus)
            else:
                from litedram.frontend.dma import LiteDRAMDMAWriter
                port = self.sdram.crossbar.get_port("write")
                self.submodules.dma_writer = LiteDRAMDMAWriter(port, fifo_depth=16, with_csr=True)

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="LiteX SoC on Arty A7")
    parser.add_argument("--toolchain",           default="vivado",                 help="Toolchain use to build (default: vivado)")
    parser.add_argument("--build",               action="store_true",              help="Build bitstream")
    parser.add_argument("--load",                action="store_true",              help="Load bitstream")
    parser.add_argument("--variant",             default="a7-35",                  help="Board variant: a7-35 (default) or a7-100")
    parser.add_argument("--sys-clk-freq",        default=100e6,                    help="System clock frequency (default: 100MHz)")
    ethopts = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    ethopts.add_argument("--with-ethernet",      action="store_true",              help="Enable Ethernet support")
    ethopts.add_argument("--with-etherbone",     action="store_true",              help="Enable Etherbone support")
    parser.add_argument("--eth-ip",              default="192.168.1.50", type=str, help="Ethernet/Etherbone IP address")
    parser.add_argument("--eth-dynamic-ip",      action="store_true",              help="Enable dynamic Ethernet IP addresses setting")
    sdopts = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    sdopts.add_argument("--with-spi-sdcard",     action="store_true",              help="Enable SPI-mode SDCard support")
    sdopts.add_argument("--with-sdcard",         action="store_true",              help="Enable SDCard support")
    parser.add_argument("--sdcard-adapter",      type=str,                         help="SDCard PMOD adapter: digilent (default) or numato")
    parser.add_argument("--with-jtagbone",       action="store_true",              help="Enable Jtagbone support")
    parser.add_argument("--with-mapped-flash",   action="store_true",              help="Enable Memory Mapped Flash")
    parser.add_argument("--with-spi-flash",      action="store_true",              help="Enable SPI Flash (MMAPed)")
    parser.add_argument("--with-pmod-gpio",      action="store_true",              help="Enable GPIOs through PMOD") # FIXME: Temporary test.
    builder_args(parser)
    soc_core_args(parser)
    vivado_build_args(parser)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    assert not (args.with_etherbone and args.eth_dynamic_ip)

    soc = BaseSoC(
        variant        = args.variant,
        toolchain      = args.toolchain,
        sys_clk_freq   = int(float(args.sys_clk_freq)),
        with_ethernet  = args.with_ethernet,
        with_etherbone = args.with_etherbone,
        eth_ip         = args.eth_ip,
        eth_dynamic_ip = args.eth_dynamic_ip,
        with_jtagbone  = args.with_jtagbone,
        with_mapped_flash = args.with_mapped_flash,
        with_spi_flash = args.with_spi_flash,
        with_pmod_gpio = args.with_pmod_gpio,
        **soc_core_argdict(args)
    )
    if args.sdcard_adapter == "numato":
        soc.platform.add_extension(arty._numato_sdcard_pmod_io)
    else:
        soc.platform.add_extension(arty._sdcard_pmod_io)
    if args.with_spi_sdcard:
        soc.add_spi_sdcard()
    if args.with_sdcard:
        soc.add_sdcard()
    builder = Builder(soc, **builder_argdict(args))
    builder_kwargs = vivado_build_argdict(args) if args.toolchain == "vivado" else {}
    builder.build(**builder_kwargs, run=args.build)

    if args.load:
        prog = soc.platform.create_programmer()
        prog.load_bitstream(os.path.join(builder.gateware_dir, soc.build_name + ".bit"))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

@suarezvictor: Thanks for reporting and sorry for the delay, this is fixed with https://github.com/enjoy-digital/litex/issues/1198. The issue was that the depth checks were done in FPGA logic, not in Python and this was generating invalid logic. I haven't noticed this when merging the 16-bit support PR. This should now be fine (at least compiles fine).

title: microwatt BIOS hangs in ISR
body:
With the current LiteX versions and the Microwatt CPU (`--cpu-type=microwatt --cpu-variant=standard+ghdl+irq`) the BIOS hangs in the ISR with what appears to be a wild jump to an invalid address outside of the memory space.  This in turn results in no console output and is repeatable in simulation.

I've attached a simulation trace database and the BIOS files generated from a Debian Bullseye ppc64le host system for analysis.  The last instructions executed appear to be as follows:

```
        /* Load IRQ handler address from SRAM */
        LOAD_IMM64(%r3, __isr_address)
    102c:       00 00 60 3c     lis     r3,0
    1030:       00 00 63 60     ori     r3,r3,0

comments.body: May be related to #1077
@shenki Any chance you might be able to take a look at this?

From what I can tell, objdump might be mistranslating `bctrl`, microwatt is processing that instruction as a `bcctr` (not sure which is correct right now, so I'm assuming microwatt is doing the right thing).

If true, the invalid jump is caused by `ld      r3,0(r3)` loading the data at 0x0 into r3, which is obviously incorrect.  Starting to suspect `__isr_address` might be wrong at this point.

Confirmed, `LOAD_IMM64(%r3, __isr_address)` is loading 0x0 (ROM base) instead of the correct location 0x100000 (SRAM base).

When run without IRQ support the console does come up, but there are residual issues that may be caused by related linking errors.  Will continue to debug here.

OK, it appears this has been an issue for quite a while and no one was testing, including on our side, as we were using a different boot firmware that takes advantage of the `SPR_KAISB` feature.

I'll be spending some time to apply https://gitlab.raptorengineering.com/kestrel-collaboration/kestrel-firmware/bootrom/-/merge_requests/10 to the LiteX tree and creating a new pull request once I know it's working...

Thanks @madscientist159, it's planned to add Microwatt testing to the CI (at it is currently done for most supported RISC-V CPUs), but this hasn't been done yet but we could put more efforts into this.

This should now be covered by current LiteX.

I also tested the Microwatt IRQ boot path locally with both:

  - `--cpu-variant=standard+irq`
  - `--cpu-variant=standard+ghdl+irq`

Both reached the LiteX BIOS prompt, so I can no longer reproduce the original ISR hang.

CI has also been updated with enjoy-digital/litex@de10ffc154a66c1798943f3070101d2825611061 so `test_cpu[microwatt]` now exercises the `standard+irq` variant directly.

I think this can now be closed. If an IRQ-specific Microwatt boot issue still reproduces on current LiteX, please open a fresh issue with the updated reproducer.

title: liblitedram accessors change causes build failure on ecp5 boards
body:
Some combination of commit 58fda1a3 ("liblitedram: Move PHY accessors to a separate file") and/or commit 4c605020 ("liblitedram: Codebase cleanup") result in a failure to build on ecp5 boards (tested on trellisboard and ecpix5):

```
riscv64-unknown-elf/bin/ld: ../liblitedram/liblitedram.a(accessors.o): in function `write_inc_dq_bitslip':
/litex/litex/soc/software/liblitedram/accessors.c:116: undefined reference to `ddrphy_wdly_dq_bitslip_write'
riscv64-unknown-elf/12.2.0/../../../../riscv64-unknown-elf/bin/ld: ../liblitedram/liblitedram.a(accessors.o): in function `write_rst_dq_bitslip':
/litex/litex/soc/software/liblitedram/accessors.c:122: undefined reference to `ddrphy_wdly_dq_bitslip_rst_write'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

From a cursory analysis it appears that the new conditional:

```
+#if defined(SDRAM_PHY_BITSLIPS)
```

doesn't adequately cover the conditions existent on ecp5 boards, whereas the old one:

```
-#if defined(SDRAM_PHY_WRITE_LATENCY_CALIBRATION_CAPABLE) || defined(SDRAM_BITSLIP_CAPABLE)
```

did. Test/debug using the following command line:

```
litex-boards/litex_boards/targets/lambdaconcept_ecpix5.py --build --cpu-type vexriscv
```

The cpu type doesn't really matter, it's the conditional compilation of accessors depending on register accessors generated in `build/lambdaconcept_ecpix5/software/include/generated/csr.h` that appears to be the problem.

@mtdudek @michalsieron @enjoy-digital -- can you double-check the `#ifdef` magic changes acrosss these commits? Thanks!

fix_commits.messageHeadline: software/liblitedram/accessors: Fix conditions for write_dq_bitslip f…

comments.body:
I decided to try pair coding with Claude to make the manual changes I mentioned above into a fully complete, but optional, feature. You can see the changes on my branches here:

* litex: https://github.com/enjoy-digital/litex/compare/master...yusefkarim:litex:yosys_wrapper_slang_option_and_ibex_regfile_option
* litex-boards: https://github.com/litex-hub/litex-boards/compare/master...yusefkarim:litex-boards:tang_nano_ibex_regfile_option 

I'm very new to the hardware world and even newer to LiteX and friends...so there's a high chance these changes are unpractical for merging into master. However, I have confirmed that it does in fact work for me and I can upload to my board without troubles with these changes. Happy to open PRs and get proper feedback for merging if desired. Thanks!

Thanks for the report and for testing the slang route.

I've opened #2510 with a smaller LiteX-side version of this:
- YosysWrapper can optionally route SystemVerilog sources through read_slang, while keeping read_verilog -sv as the default.
- Yosys/nextpnr now has a --yosys-slang option, and platforms can request slang/options when a core needs it.
- Ibex now requests the slang frontend internally, adds the prim flop sources needed by the elaboration, and supports platform.ibex_regfile with ff as the default and fpga as an opt-in.

I kept the board-specific register-file selection separate, so targets can opt in to the fpga register file only when needed.

- python3 -m py_compile litex/build/yosys_wrapper.py litex/build/yosys_nextpnr_toolchain.py litex/soc/cores/cpu/ibex/core.py test/build/test_yosys_wrapper.py test/cores/test_cpu_ibex.py
- git diff --check

fix_commits.messageHeadline: build/sim: define default Verilator user hooks

comments.body:
Thanks for the detailed log. The failure appears to come from the optional Verilator user hooks used by the LiteX simulator:

```
litex_sim_user_init
litex_sim_user_pre_eval
litex_sim_user_post_eval
```

These were declared as undefined weak symbols so user code could optionally provide them. That can still leave unresolved symbols at final link on Darwin/arm64 when no user hook source is provided, which matches the linker error in your log.

I opened a fix here:
https://github.com/enjoy-digital/litex/pull/2509

The PR provides weak no-op default definitions for these hooks, while still allowing user-provided strong definitions through `--verilator-extra-source` to override them.

Tested with:
